claim: UALVP 2 was collected in 1921 during the University of Alberta field program.
source: University of Alberta Dino Lab history

claim: UALVP 2 is described institutionally as the most complete Stegoceras specimen to date in the historical record.
source: University of Alberta Dino Lab history
fem_uq_consequence: Supports specimen primacy; does not eliminate preparation distortion

claim: UALVP 2 includes a nearly complete skull, both lower jaws, and parts of the postcranial skeleton.
UALVP 2 is a principal comparative basis for Stegoceras and conforms to the type frontoparietal.
UALVP 2 was CT-scanned and used in comparative cranial biomechanics.
Cortical density/thickness increases toward the dome apex.
A lower-density trabecular region lies beneath dense cortical bone; trabeculae broadly radiate perpendicular to the outer dome.
fem_uq_consequence: Internal architecture may alter stiffness/stress paths

claim: A dense deep compact layer is present.
fem_uq_consequence: Homogeneous material model is a substantive simplification

claim: Numerous canals/tubular structures connect toward the cranial surface.
Beam hardening may inflate apparent superficial density; a dense deep compact layer remained evident.
The 2011 UALVP 2 model used a 1360 N impact load.
fem_uq_consequence: Benchmark load case; not unique biological force

claim: The 2011 model included bone and keratin tissue types.
The 2011 study compared UALVP 2 with Prenocephale and extant artiodactyl crania.
Stegoceras shares dome morphology, surface canals, neck muscle attachments and layered cranial bone with extant head-strike correlates.
fem_uq_consequence: Motivates but does not prove impact scenario

claim: The model reported lower stress/higher safety-factor behavior for Stegoceras than several comparison taxa under its chosen loading.
Stegoceras dome morphology changes strongly through ontogeny.
The ontogenetic pattern is continuous and quantitatively modeled rather than a simple flat-vs-domed dichotomy.
22% of sampled pachycephalosaurid specimens had dome lesions; lesions clustered near the apex.
fem_uq_consequence: Independent evidence stream for impact hypotheses

claim: Authors interpreted lesion distribution as consistent with intraspecific butting.
fem_uq_consequence: Do not encode as behavioral certainty

claim: A recent review argues that “headbutting” is underspecified and that brain injury cannot be inferred solely from cranial deformation.
fem_uq_consequence: Define mechanical event and outcome criteria
